description: The one classification of every .gaia/local entry, transcribed by hand from the frozen state-model classification (never generated from code, which is what is under correction). Consumers read this instead of hand-maintaining their own lists. `path` is relative to .gaia/local/ unless the row carries `root: notebook`, in which case it is relative to <main>/.notebook (the root of specs, plans and research; `root` defaults to `local`, and a lookup matches only the rows of the root it asks for). A `path` may join more than one concrete on-disk shape with '|' when a single logical entry covers several filenames (e.g. a clearance marker's .ok/.refused siblings); each '|'-joined alternative is matched independently under the entry's own `match` rule. A `path` may also carry a '<placeholder>' token for a variable path segment (a spec id, a digest, a worktree name); for `match: glob` a placeholder behaves as a shell '*' wildcard, and for `match: prefix` only the literal text before the first '<' is significant. `residue` lists known dead-feature/legacy paths that are real on some machines but are not live state: never treated as drift and never a live entry. `bash .gaia/scripts/state-registry-lib.sh residue-sweep` lists the ones present and `--apply` deletes them. A residue row may name a `successor`, a .gaia/local-relative path its state moves to once: the sweep leaves that row's paths alone until the successor exists, so state a pending move has yet to carry is never deleted. `report_only` lists the three old notebook roots (specs/, plans/, research/ under .gaia/local): paths under one are recognized (never Unknown), listed by the sweep once per root in a section of their own, and never deleted by `--apply` at any depth, whatever a residue row beneath them says; a human reviews what the one-time move left there.

entries.keyed_by: singleton per-clone value; correct via idempotent overwrite, no partition key needed
entries.why: Per-clone /gaia-init and /setup-gaia step-completion record, plus the machine-scope setup decisions (`decisions`). A per-tree copy would re-run setup steps per worktree, which is wrong for a fact about the clone, not the tree.

entries.keyed_by: session id, two files per Claude Code session: the context reading (<session_id>.json) and the effort reading (<session_id>.effort.json)
entries.why: The statusline writes each session's context reading (<session_id>.json, tmp + mv) for the audit loop's checkpoint to read, and beside it the session's effort reading (<session_id>.effort.json, tmp + mv), which usage.sh record reads for the ledger's close rows. Anchored to the main root so every worktree's render lands in one place the bound hook finds. Must precede cache-shared, whose prefix would otherwise claim these files first.
entries.reaped_by: check-updates.sh (sweeps regular files older than 7 days on its TTL-gated pass)

entries.keyed_by: singleton machine-scoped caches, each overwritten in place; update-gaia/<tag>/ additionally partitions by release tag, and update-gaia/run/ holds the current update run's merge report and candidates and is removed by the next prune
entries.why: Machine-scoped release/update-check and statusline-guard state (update-check.json, update-gaia/<tag>/, update-gaia/run/, serena-guard/) that is a property of the machine, not of any one tree. Per-session context readings under context/ are the separate context-readings row, which precedes this one.

entries.keyed_by: singleton per machine
entries.why: Machine-local, lower-only override of the audit checkpoint's context line. Lives in the protected folder and is hand-authored by a human; Claude tool writes to it are denied by block-audit-loop-write.sh.

entries.keyed_by: singleton per machine
entries.why: GAIA's per-machine opt-ins (the statusline left-side choice). Written by /setup-gaia and read by the statusline from every tree; not write-guarded, unlike protected/checkpoint-override.json.

entries.keyed_by: branch-own digest and member, in the file name, plus the tree; the per-branch ledger is keyed by branch
entries.why: The light-review route records, reviewer inputs, verdicts and the per-branch light-review ledger. Written beside the clearance markers in the shared audit store so one gate sees every checkout's light reviews. Must precede the audit-store glob rows, whose patterns could otherwise claim files under this directory first.

entries.keyed_by: branch-own digest over the branch's own patch to the files the audited member owns (per member), bound to the branch
entries.why: A clearance marker attests a Code Audit Team member reviewed the branch's own change, measured against the PR's base branch, so content the base brought in does not rotate it; the symlinked drop zone lets one gate judge every checkout's markers.

entries.keyed_by: key base plus branch, computed by gaia_audit_key (.gaia/scripts/audit-key-lib.sh); the key base is the branch's first-parent fork point on non-anchored arms, fixed across catch-up merges, and key base alone collides across worktrees cut from one main tip
entries.why: Co-written into the symlinked audit store; the branch discriminator is the missing partition that keeps two trees' findings from overwriting each other.

entries.keyed_by: key base plus branch, computed by gaia_audit_key (.gaia/scripts/audit-key-lib.sh), plus the member -- the same partition the findings sidecar uses, and for the same reason (key base alone collides across worktrees cut from one main tip); the key base is the branch's first-parent fork point on non-anchored arms, fixed across catch-up merges
entries.why: The scope-time digest a Code Audit Team member attests to, written where the member resolves its review scope (.gaia/scripts/audit-scope-digest.sh --capture) and read back where it writes its clearance (--read), so the marker cannot attest a branch-own change that moved under the review.

entries.keyed_by: base-sha plus branch, computed by gaia_audit_key (.gaia/scripts/audit-key-lib.sh), plus the member -- the same partition the scope digests use
entries.why: The per-member review input a blend reaches the reviewer as: the branch's changed hunks since the member's anchor plus the remerge-diff of any merge commit that changed a path, so a conflict resolution is read as a diff and never as a whole file.

entries.keyed_by: HEAD sha
entries.why: Redacted local security detail, keyed by the commit it describes, in the shared audit store.

entries.keyed_by: singleton per clone; hand-authored, resolved through the main checkout
entries.why: The optional machine-local price override that pricing overlays on the distributed rate table. User-written, never reaped, and never replaced by a sync.

entries.keyed_by: singleton store; the shared cost mutex plus self-identifying rows (session_id + key + first_ts; cursor rows by session_id + role + path)
entries.why: Append-only usage ledger of segment, binding, and cursor rows. Every tree contributes, so correctness comes from the lock and the self-identifying rows, not from partitioning; attribution is resolved at read time.

entries.keyed_by: singleton store; the shared cost mutex plus self-identifying rows (edge and unlink rows by child + parent + ts; merge rows by pr + key)
entries.why: Append-only lineage ledger of edge, unlink, and merge rows. Written by any tree under the same mutex as the usage ledger; readers apply tombstones at read time.

entries.keyed_by: singleton store; append-only rows that identify themselves by branch, member and digest
entries.why: Maintainer-repo-only log of each light-review routing decision, appended by the routing telemetry script and read by its tally. It does not exist on an adopter clone.

entries.keyed_by: singleton per clone; temp-file-then-rename under the mutex
entries.why: Regenerable cache folded from the usage ledger's cursor rows: the latest offset per transcript file. Deleting it re-reads from the ledger, never loses a row.

entries.keyed_by: singleton per clone; temp-file-then-rename, lock-free, last writer wins
entries.why: Regenerable cache of branch-name derivations and per-store read offsets for the usage readouts. Deleting it, or any corruption, only makes the next readout derive from scratch; it holds no attribution.

entries.keyed_by: singleton per clone; atomic mkdir
entries.why: Singleton guard for the SessionStart transcript sweep, so two sessions starting together do not both parse the backlog.

entries.keyed_by: one mktemp name per write, never reused
entries.why: In-flight temp files of the usage writers, present between creation and the rename or append. A process killed mid-write can leave one behind; it is inert (nothing reads it). Only the branch memo's temps have a reaper; every other writer's temps have none.
entries.reaped_by: usage.sh readouts reap .usage-branch-memo.tmp.* older than 60 s; other writers' temps have none

entries.keyed_by: singleton; idempotent overwrite of a cache whose authority is a repo-global GitHub fact
entries.why: A worktree debt fix must arm main's count cache, not a discarded per-tree copy; the authority is the GitHub tech-debt label, not this file.

entries.keyed_by: the tree key (gaia_tree_key, .gaia/scripts/main-root-lib.sh): the first 16 hex characters of a sha256 over this working tree's physically-resolved root. The entry addresses itself at red-ledger/<tree_key>/, so it stays private to its tree once .gaia/local is shared.
entries.why: A RED observation is a claim about one working tree at one commit; sharing it across trees would be a category error. The identity rule's own reference example of correctly per-tree state.

entries.keyed_by: the tree key (gaia_tree_key, .gaia/scripts/main-root-lib.sh): the first 16 hex characters of a sha256 over this working tree's physically-resolved root. The entry addresses itself at worthiness-ledger/<tree_key>/, so it stays private to its tree once .gaia/local is shared.
entries.why: A worthiness observation is a claim about one working tree's emergent-surface tests at one commit, the same kind of per-tree fact as a RED observation. It lives under worthiness-ledger/, outside the wholesale-symlinked audit/ segment, so it is per-tree by the same mechanism as its RED-ledger sibling: gaia_registry_linkable_paths only symlinks scope:"shared" entries, and this one is not.

entries.keyed_by: the tree key (gaia_tree_key, .gaia/scripts/main-root-lib.sh): the first 16 hex characters of a sha256 over this working tree's physically-resolved root. The entry addresses itself at forensics/<tree_key>/, so it stays private to its tree once .gaia/local is shared.
entries.why: A human-facing local forensics report read in the checkout that produced it; no cross-tree consumer. Named in the write-guard's own non-exempt list.

entries.keyed_by: singleton per-clone ledger keyed internally by finding_class; atomic replace without a cross-tree lock, so simultaneous writes can drop one decline and re-offer that candidate
entries.why: The operator's declines on the machine's codify candidates. The candidate set is the repo's merged-PR window and the nudge it feeds is machine-scoped, so one copy per clone is the only scope at which a decline can suppress what it declined. Shared through the registry-driven symlink, so a decline recorded in a linked worktree lands in the main checkout's copy and survives that worktree's removal.

entries.keyed_by: singleton per-clone snapshot; atomic replace, so a review completed in one tree unconditionally supersedes another's
entries.why: What a completed /gaia-codify review saw: the audited-PR denominator, the class inventory, and when it ran, plus the start-of-run tally it was built from. The nudge it silences is machine-scoped like the decline ledger, so one copy per clone is the only scope at which a review can discharge what it reviewed. Shared through the registry-driven symlink, so a review completed in a linked worktree lands in the main checkout's copy and survives that worktree's removal.
The SPEC-number allocation's authority is the remote immutable spec/NNN tag; the ledger is main's cache and the plan reference contracts the SPEC-NNN folders to the main checkout.
The plan folder stays in the main checkout by contract; worktree-mode orchestrators write PROGRESS.md back to main.

GAIA's documented research location. A research Write under the main checkout's research directory binds the session's default-branch spend at read time, so the directory must resolve to main's copy from every tree.
The notebook's one index of specs, plans and research. Only the notebook library reads or writes it, under its catalog write lock; every other script goes through the library.

A PR-capture written under main's cache for the merge flow, main-anchored not per-tree, and partitioned per-branch in the filename (cache/gh-artifact-pr.<branch-slug>.json) so two worktrees opening PRs concurrently no longer share one unkeyed last-writer-wins file. Still main-only rather than shared: worktrees reach this file by resolving main's root, they are never given their own linked copy, so keyed_by stays null per the schema's rule and the key shows up in `path` instead.

The residue triage command's derived read cache (per-pull-request attribution and resolved cited lines, keyed by pull-request number and head sha) and its resumable per-run cursor. Derived state, never a record: a cold cache reproduces the same candidate list. Main-only rather than shared, so keyed_by stays null per the schema's rule and the two concrete filenames show up in `path` instead. Named `residual`, not `residue`: this registry's own top-level `residue` array names an unrelated concept, orphaned machine-local state with no automatic reaper.

Per-branch audit loop history and allowance, resolved to main so every session, sub-agent, fork and linked worktree on the branch reads one record. Lives in the protected folder; written only by the audit loop hooks.

Per-branch record that the maintainer harness verification passed for a commit, resolved to main so the audit loop hook reads one record from every tree. Written by the verification runner, read by the audit loop bound hook; a project without the maintainer test tree never writes it.

One identity per clone, used in ping/telemetry. Forks per worktree path today via a hash of the repo root path, a defect; classified at its main-only target scope with the fix deferred to a later phase.
An update-preference file written only from main in the shipped workflow, because the /update-deps flow refuses to run from a linked worktree before any write happens.
Read-anchored to main (the statusline command resolves to main) or operator-authored per machine; single copies with no per-tree meaning. Hand-authored, not GAIA-generated.
Per-machine markers (a sandbox-resolution result, a short-lived setup sentinel); one value per clone.
The live in-flight SPEC draft, its pre-dispatch retry snapshots, and the gate-1 drift-detection snapshot for one authoring session; keyed by spec id, deleted at canonical save or on discard.
Per-tree session shape (start time, Socratic question-ceiling counter) for one SPEC-authoring session; the holder's own working state, keyed by spec id, stays where it is written.
The session-host liveness lock for one SPEC-authoring session; deliberately resolved to main so the cross-tree mutex is reachable from both trees, keyed by spec id.
Self-review and adversarial-audit scratch (per-lens findings, refutation verdicts, coverage log) for one in-progress SPEC-authoring session; keyed by spec id, deleted at canonical save or discard.

One Code Audit Team member's private working copy for the one kind of evidence that needs real bytes on disk: breaking a construct a guard names to establish the guard is not hollow. Each member invocation mints its child with mktemp under a member-name prefix, which keeps co-dispatched members and concurrent audits from other worktrees out of each other's tree, and removes exactly that child when done.
gaia-react-perf measurement run output, keyed by run id.
Transient gh-issue-body staging files, keyed by run stamp, self-pruned by their producer in the shared audit directory.

/gaia-cleanse findings reports, the filing outcomes it hands the tech-debt filer, and the filer's retry records beside them, keyed by timestamp/run stamp and self-pruned by their producer. The newest applied report's mtime anchors the statusline cleanse nudge.

entries.keyed_by: the normalized branch key with its branch: prefix dropped (slashes nest), or session-<session id> for a detached HEAD; one folder per key, never shared between keys
entries.why: Execution-doctrine run folder (STATE.md checkpoint, findings, log.md) written by Claude through Bash while a branch or worktree session runs. Shared so a worktree's folder lands in the one main-anchored store and a resumed session finds it from any tree. Small; a reaper is a filed follow-up, so reaped_by is null for now.

entries.keyed_by: tree root, one line per linked worktree; read-modify-write under a cross-tree mkdir lock, written temp-then-mv
entries.why: The main-anchored slot ledger: which linked worktree holds which port slot. One ledger for every tree is the point, so two worktrees can never be handed the same ports.
entries.reaped_by: slot reclaim in worktree provisioning and in the ports session-start cleanup

entries.keyed_by: tree root, one line per linked worktree a post-merge cleanup kept (tree, branch, why); a second stop of the same tree replaces its line, written temp-then-mv
entries.why: The worktree removal check records each tree it stops removing, so the session-start reminder can list it until it is removed. Main-anchored so every tree reads and writes one ledger.
entries.reaped_by: the kept-worktree reminder (kept-worktrees.sh remind) drops the line of a tree git no longer lists as a live worktree

entries.keyed_by: Claude Code session id, one file per session holding the tree root it last provisioned or entered
entries.why: Lets the kept-worktree reminder leave out a tree a live Claude session is working in. Main-anchored so a session in any tree is seen from every other.
entries.reaped_by: the ports dead-session reap (gaia_server_reap_dead_sessions) deletes a session's record with its host record once the host has exited; the kept-worktree reminder also deletes the record of a tree it checks whose host has exited

entries.keyed_by: one file per retired ledger entry, named <slot>.<epoch>.tsv
entries.why: A reclaimed slot's leftover servers must still be found and stopped after the ledger line is gone. One file per entry means a reaper deletes it with rm and never rewrites a shared file.
entries.reaped_by: the tombstone reap once no listener on the slot's ports qualifies for a removed-tree stop, or after 7 days

entries.why: A singleton mkdir lock serializing ledger rewrites across trees, with no partition key. Held only for the read-modify-write, never across a signal or a wait.
entries.reaped_by: broken once when older than 60 seconds

entries.keyed_by: server PID, one file per server a Claude session launched
entries.why: Records which dev or Storybook server a Claude session started, with its process identity, so a dead session's server can be stopped after the identity is re-verified. A human's launch is never recorded.
entries.reaped_by: the dead-session reap (ports session-start cleanup and worktree provisioning); the tombstone reap prunes the records of a reclaimed tree

entries.keyed_by: Claude Code session id, one file per session
entries.why: Records each live session's host process so a launch can be attributed to it and a dead host can be told from a live one.
entries.reaped_by: the dead-session reap, when the host is dead and no launch record names the session

entries.why: Per-session dedupe marker written by workflow-doctrine-inject.sh (tmp + mv, through Bash) holding the last injected key so startup, resume and tool events do not re-inject an unchanged doctrine. Anchored to the main root, never the entered tree. One tiny file per session; a reaper is a filed follow-up, so reaped_by is null for now.

Per-session marker written by context-checkpoint-inject.sh (tmp + mv) holding the highest context band the checkpoint has fired for, so each band fires once per session. Anchored to the main root so a session moving between the main checkout and a worktree sees one marker.
entries.reaped_by: check-updates.sh (sweeps regular files older than 7 days on its TTL-gated pass)

entries.why: Per-sub-agent marker written by context-checkpoint-subagent.sh (tmp + mv) holding the sub-agent's handoff opt-in and the highest context band the checkpoint has fired for, so each band fires once per sub-agent. Anchored to the main root so a sub-agent running in a worktree sees one marker.
entries.reaped_by: check-updates.sh (sweeps regular files older than 7 days on its TTL-gated pass)

residue.why: Opt-in config for the removed mentorship feature; a stray one has no reaper.
Removed mentorship feature's cloud event stream.
Removed mentorship feature's analytics reports.
Orphaned marker from the removed mentorship feature; both its writer and reader are gone.
Residue pattern from a deleted carry-forward feature; no current writer anywhere in the codebase, and no reaper if one is ever found.
Residue pattern from a deleted out-of-scope disposition sidecar; no current writer anywhere in the codebase, and no reaper if one is ever found.
Per-checkout sentinel from a removed feature's one-time cleanup pass; transitional residue with no live writer.
Per-tree session handoff files from the removed handoff and pickup commands; no live writer and no reaper.
Retired cost ledger; the file stays on disk unread and has no writer.
Retired seeded rate table; the file stays on disk unread and has no writer. Pricing reads the distributed table plus the override.
Retired rate-table merge base; the file stays on disk unread and has no writer.
Retired byte copy of the distributed rate table; the file stays on disk unread and has no writer.
Retired rate-feed backoff record; the file stays on disk unread and has no writer.
Retired preserved copies of an unreadable seeded rate table; the files stay on disk unread and have no writer or reaper.

The old state directory of the command now named /gaia-codify. The CLI moves it to codify/ once and leaves it behind when codify/ already exists or when it holds a ledger in a format codify no longer reads; nothing reads it afterwards.
Reports left in audit/ when a report of the same name already sits in cleanse/; the one-time move never overwrites. Nothing reads them afterwards.
Retired in-flight temp files of the seeded rate table writes; any found is inert and has no writer or reaper.
Machine-local config of the removed GAIA CI automation; nothing reads or writes it.
Logs of removed features (spec pacing, the spec-to-issue mirror, the audit re-spawn measurement); nothing reads or writes them.
Backups of the retired cost ledger; nothing reads them.
Run and archive folders of the removed /health-audit; nothing reads or writes them.

Cycle folders and the moved-aside previous audit folder of the removed /health-audit; nothing reads or writes them. The cycle shapes stop at two digits so a digest-named marker that starts with c never matches.
Backups and a probe file the 1.6.1 worktree linker left when it replaced real state with a symlink; nothing reads them.

1.6.1 clearance markers, keyed by a 40-hex commit id. Current markers are keyed by a 64-hex digest, so one of this exact shape is never read; the glob spells forty hex digits so no current marker matches it.

Scratch of removed audit steps (progress breadcrumbs, wave stamps, the disposition sidecar's temp files) and the earlier worthiness log location, now per tree under worthiness-ledger/; nothing reads or writes them here.
State of the removed spec-to-plan chain guard and the removed spec-kit version-check throttle; nothing reads or writes them.

report_only.why: SPEC folders and ledger of the pre-notebook layout. The one-time move carries them to the notebook; what it keeps (collision copies, archived/ layouts, the frozen ledger backup) stays here for a human to review.
Plan folders and ledger of the pre-notebook layout, including slug-named plan folders and archived/ layouts the one-time move keeps; a human reviews what remains.
Research folders of the pre-notebook layout. The one-time move carries them to the notebook; anything left is for a human to review.

rm_whitelist.why: Individual plan folders are clearable by an agent, but the notebook's plans folder is main-anchored state that is never bulk-deleted, so only its children are whitelisted.
Individual spec folders are clearable, but the notebook's specs folder is the main-anchored SPEC store and is never bulk-deleted; children only.
Audit markers and reports are self-pruning scratch; the shared audit/ store is symlinked structure that is never bulk-deleted; children only.
Cleanse reports are self-pruning scratch the /gaia-cleanse playbook ages out; the cleanse/ container is kept, only its children are cleared.
Cache entries are regenerable machine/session scratch; the cache/ container is kept, only its contents are cleared.
Per-branch run folders and their dispatch artifacts are scratch the PR Merge Workflow pre-clears by absolute path before each dispatch; the runs/ container is kept, only its contents are cleared.

The short-lived sentinel /setup-gaia creates to stand down the main-branch commit guard and removes with rm -f once its commit lands; a leftover keeps that guard suspended, so its removal must pass in the absolute spelling shell-cwd.md prescribes.
Build output regenerated by the build; safe to remove wholesale (rm -rf dist), so the directory itself and its children are both whitelisted. Repo-root-relative, outside .gaia/local.
Build output regenerated by the build; safe to remove wholesale, directory and children alike. Repo-root-relative, outside .gaia/local.
